verses.text: When the uproar ended, Paul sent for the disciples. After encouraging them and saying goodbye, he set out for Macedonia.
He traveled through that region, encouraging the believers with many words, and then arrived in Greece.
He stayed there three months. Just as he was about to sail for Syria, the Jews plotted against him, so he decided to return through Macedonia.
His traveling companions included Sopater from Berea; Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica; Gaius from Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia.
They went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.
After the Festival of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi and met them in Troas five days later. We stayed there for seven days.
On the first day of the week, we gathered to break bread. Paul spoke to the people, planning to leave the next day, and kept talking until midnight.
There were many lamps in the upstairs room where we were gathered.
A young man named Eutychus was sitting in the window. As Paul kept talking, Eutychus sank into a deep sleep, fell from the third floor, and was picked up dead.
Paul went down, bent over him, and held him close. “Don’t panic,” he said. “He’s alive.”
Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. He talked with them until dawn, then left.
They took the young man home alive and were deeply comforted.
We went ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we planned to pick Paul up. He had arranged to travel there by land.
When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
We sailed from there and the next day passed Chios. The day after that we reached Samos, stopped at Trogyllium, and the following day arrived in Miletus.
Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so he wouldn’t lose time in Asia. He was hurrying to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by Pentecost.
From Miletus he sent a message to Ephesus, calling the church elders to meet him.
When they arrived, he said, “You know how I lived among you from the first day I set foot in Asia.
“I served the Lord with humility, tears, and the hardships that came from the Jews’ plots against me.
“You know I never held back from telling you anything that would help you. I taught you in public and from house to house.
“I urged both Jews and Greeks to turn to God and put their faith in our Lord Jesus.
“Now I’m going to Jerusalem, compelled by the Spirit. I don’t know what will happen to me there.
“I only know that in every city the Holy Spirit warns me that prison and suffering are waiting for me.
“But my life means nothing to me unless I can finish my race and complete the work the Lord Jesus gave me: to testify to the good news of God’s grace.
“Now I know that none of you, among whom I traveled preaching God’s Kingdom, will ever see me again.
“So today I can say that I’m not responsible for anyone’s lost life,
because I didn’t hold back from telling you everything God wanted you to know.
“Watch yourselves and the whole flock. The Holy Spirit appointed you as leaders to care for God’s church, which he bought with his own blood.
“I know that after I leave, savage wolves will come among you and won’t spare the flock.
“Even some of you will twist the truth to pull disciples away and get them to follow you.
“So stay alert. Remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you, night and day, with tears.
“Now I entrust you to God and to the message of his grace. It can build you up and give you the inheritance shared by all who belong to God.
“I never coveted anyone’s silver, gold, or clothing.
“You know these hands worked to provide for my needs and for the people with me.
In every way I showed you how to work hard and help those who are weak. Remember what the Lord Jesus said: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.”
After saying this, Paul knelt down and prayed with them all.
They all cried openly, hugged Paul, and kissed him.
What grieved them most was his saying they would never see him again. Then they walked with him to the ship.
